generated_note: Values marked 'sourced' were seen in SciSpace MCP tool output on 2026-11-21 (per-m3 CO2 figures were converted to per-kg by dividing by a typical density; see each material's notes). Values marked 'typical' are handbook-level figures not seen in tool output tonight. Ratings 1-5 are AI-assigned judgments.

materials.name: Normal-strength Portland cement concrete (~30 MPa)
materials.humidity_reason: Hydrated cement paste is stable when wet, but its capillary porosity lets moisture, CO2 and chlorides reach and corrode embedded steel over time.
materials.wear_reason: Moderate abrasion resistance that depends on aggregate hardness and surface finish; ordinary paste dusts and wears under heavy traffic.
materials.main_limitation: Low tensile strength (needs steel reinforcement) and a cement-driven carbon footprint.
materials.notes: Embodied CO2 is a unit conversion: sourced 290-320 kg CO2-e/m3 (midpoint 305) divided by a typical density of 2400 kg/m3 = 0.127 kg/kg, rounded to 0.13.

sources.citation: Flower, D.J.M. and Sanjayan, J.G., 2007, Green house gas emissions due to concrete manufacture, International Journal of Life Cycle Assessment
sources.quote: Typical normal-strength concrete using Portland cement as the sole binder emits 0.29-0.32 t CO2-e per m3 (290-320 kg CO2-e/m3). [SciSpace extract_data summary of the paper]

materials.name: High-strength concrete (~70 MPa)
materials.humidity_reason: Low water-to-binder ratio gives a dense, low-permeability matrix that slows moisture and chloride ingress, though reinforcement still needs cover.
materials.wear_reason: Abrasion resistance rises with compressive strength and paste density, so it wears more slowly than normal concrete.
materials.main_limitation: High cement content raises embodied CO2 per kg, and the dense matrix is brittle and prone to explosive spalling in fire.
materials.notes: Embodied CO2 is a handbook-level estimate (about 450-500 kg cement per m3 at roughly 0.9 kg CO2 per kg cement, divided by 2450 kg/m3); no per-kg figure for a plain 70 MPa mix was seen in tool output tonight.

sources.citation: Zende, A.A., Momin, A.I.A., Alsabhan, A.H. et al., 2023, Mechanical Properties of High-Strength Self-Compacting Concrete, ACS Omega
sources.quote: Three mixes were selected, having compressive strengths of more than 70, 80, and 90 MPa, respectively.

sources.citation: Burg, R.G. and Ost, B.W., 1994, Engineering properties of commercially available high-strength concretes (including three-year data), Portland Cement Association report
sources.quote: Six concretes in the range of 10,000 to 20,000 psi (69 to 138 MPa) were studied.

materials.name: Ultra-high-performance concrete (UHPC)
materials.humidity_reason: Very low water-to-binder ratio and optimised particle packing leave almost no connected capillary porosity for water or chlorides to enter.
materials.wear_reason: Very dense, high-strength matrix with fine hard quartz filler resists abrasion well.
materials.main_limitation: Very high binder content makes it costly and carbon-intensive per kg, and it needs careful mixing and curing.
materials.notes: Embodied CO2 is a unit conversion: the upper end of the sourced range (812.8 kg CO2-e/m3) divided by a typical density of 2450 kg/m3 = 0.33 kg/kg. The source mixes are silica-fume-free and the range runs down to 570.3 kg/m3 (0.23 kg/kg); steel fibres would add to this.

sources.citation: Magureanu, C., Sosa, I., Negrutiu, C. et al., 2012, Mechanical Properties and Durability of Ultra-High-Performance Concrete, Materials
sources.quote: UHPC can achieve a compressive strength of approximately 150 N/mm2 (21,756 psi) and a modulus of elasticity greater than 50,000 N/mm2

sources.citation: Sifan, M., Nagaratnam, B., Railton, J. et al., 2026, Silica-fume-free UHPC with basalt, dolomite and limestone: fresh and hardened properties and embodied carbon characteristics, Magazine of Concrete Research
sources.quote: high compressive strength (190.7 MPa), and reduced embodied carbon (570.3-812.8 kgEC/m3)

sources.citation: Choi, D., Hong, K., Ochirbud, M. et al., 2023, Mechanical Properties of UHPC and UHPFRC with Recycled Sand, International Journal of Concrete Structures and Materials
sources.quote: achieving compressive strength of 128 MPa and elastic modulus of 46.9 GPa

materials.name: Geopolymer concrete (fly ash / slag based)
materials.humidity_reason: The reported water absorption is lower than conventional concrete, but alkali leaching can cause efflorescence in damp conditions.
materials.wear_reason: Abrasion resistance is broadly comparable to Portland cement concrete of the same strength grade.
materials.main_limitation: Needs caustic alkali activators, lacks mature design standards, and depends on fly ash and slag supply.
materials.notes: Embodied CO2 is labelled typical because it is an estimate, not a number seen directly: the sourced 40-80% reduction (midpoint 60%) applied to the sourced OPC concrete baseline of about 0.127 kg/kg gives about 0.05 kg/kg (range 0.025-0.076). No numeric water absorption was returned by the tools; only the qualitative finding that it is lower than conventional concrete.

sources.citation: Nagajothi, S., Elavenil, S., Angalaeswari, S. et al., 2022, Durability Studies on Fly Ash Based Geopolymer Concrete Incorporated with Slag and Alkali Solutions, Advances in Civil Engineering
sources.quote: the durability of G30 grade geopolymer concrete has been investigated using tests acid resistance, water absorption, sulphate resistance, Rapid Chloride Penetration Test (RCPT), and rate of absorption (Sorptivity) test

sources.citation: Sureshkumar, P., 2026, Low-carbon and Geopolymer Concrete: Advances, Challenges, and Future Directions (review)
sources.quote: highlighting CO2 reductions of 40-80% and comparable compressive strengths

sources.citation: Sorathiya, D.R., Khoker, P., Sain, R. et al., 2025, Study on the Effect of Geopolymer Concrete in Reducing Carbon Footprint
sources.quote: comparable or superior compressive strength and up to 80% lower CO2 emissions compared to traditional OPC concrete

materials.name: Fired clay brick
materials.humidity_reason: The fired ceramic body is chemically stable in wet air, but its high open porosity takes up water and can suffer frost damage and efflorescence.
materials.wear_reason: The sintered body is hard but porous and brittle, so edges and faces chip and erode under abrasion.
materials.main_limitation: Brittle and weak in tension, with energy-intensive kiln firing at around 900-1100 C.
materials.notes: Density is from a plain (no additive) control brick. Strength and water absorption are the midpoints of ranges reported for clay bricks containing 10-30% dolomite powder fired at 1000 C, so treat them as representative of fired clay brick rather than of one plain product.

sources.citation: Abadir, M.F., Abd El-razik, M.M., El-Naggar, K.A.M. et al., 2022, Performance assessment of fired bricks incorporating pomegranate peels waste, Innovative Infrastructure Solutions
sources.quote: Control/reference brick (0% pomegranate peel waste): Bulk density was 1,715 kg/m3 at 900 C and 1,720 kg/m3 at 1,000 C. [SciSpace extract_data summary of the paper]

sources.citation: Kizinievic, O., Kizinievic, V., Skamat, J. et al., 2023, Characteristics of fired clay bricks with dolomite powder addition, Steklo i Keramika (Glass and Ceramics)
sources.quote: clay bricks density is 1.55 - 1.75 g/m3, compressive strength 14 - 28 MPa, water absorption 15.3 - 19.7 %, total porosity 31,0 - 40.4 %

materials.name: Soda-lime float glass
materials.humidity_reason: Non-porous and impervious to water; only slow surface weathering occurs under prolonged stagnant condensation.
materials.wear_reason: Harder than most metals, but silica grit scratches it and surface flaws sharply reduce its strength.
materials.main_limitation: Brittle with low, flaw-controlled tensile strength and poor thermal-shock resistance unless tempered.
materials.notes: Modulus and hardness were measured on commercial soda-lime-silica cover slip glass (same glass family, thin sheet rather than float plate). Hardness is a unit conversion of the sourced 4.46 GPa Vickers hardness (4460 MPa / 9.807 = 455 HV); handbook values for float glass are often somewhat higher.

sources.citation: Seal, A., Dalui, A.K., Banerjee, M. et al., 2001, Mechanical properties of very thin cover slip glass disk, Bulletin of Materials Science
sources.quote: Young's modulus: 72.4 GPa by biaxial flexure with LVDT measurement; 84.9 GPa by ultrasonic measurement. Vickers hardness: 4.46 GPa (about 5-20 N indentation load). [SciSpace extract_data summary of the paper]
